title: Read the shape

dx.label: THE DIAGNOSIS
dx.name: Rebreathing
dx.text: Inspired gas should contain no CO2. An inspiratory baseline above zero means exhaled CO2 is being breathed back in.

items: **Raised inspiratory baseline:** rebreathing. Check for exhausted CO2 absorbent and a stuck or incompetent unidirectional valve.
**Slow upstroke, sloped plateau:** expiratory obstruction, such as bronchospasm or a kinked tube.
**Notch in the plateau:** spontaneous breaths as neuromuscular blockade wears off (curare cleft).
**Sudden EtCO2 drop with unchanged ventilation:** less blood flow to the lungs, such as an embolism or a sharp fall in cardiac output.
! Low cardiac output and high CO2 production change the waveform's height. Neither puts CO2 in inspired gas.

title: Pay and structure
items: **W-2 or 1099?** As a 1099 contractor you usually pay both halves of Social Security and Medicare tax, and you get no employer health insurance, retirement match or paid leave.
**Call:** how often, in-house or from home, and is it paid separately?
**Late stays:** how are hours past your scheduled shift paid?

title: Why the retry matters
paras: In a randomized trial of **40 pediatric and emergency medicine residents**, repeated testing beat repeated studying of the same material **six months later**: **39% vs 26%** on the final test.
Spacing the retry out over days adds to the effect.

title: Why D

dx.label: THE PROBLEM
dx.name: A full stomach
dx.text: His labs are corrected, so he is ready for surgery. But the pylorus is blocked: secretions and barium stay in the stomach, even with an NG tube.

items: A **14 Fr multi-orifice orogastric tube** passed just before induction recovered an average of **4.8 mL/kg**, about 96% of the fluid in the stomach.
Those volumes **weren't reduced** by NG suction, fasting time or a prior barium study.
Then intubate after **RSI or modified RSI**. Awake intubation took longer and failed more often on the first attempt.
! Metoclopramide can't empty a stomach through a blocked pylorus. Famotidine doesn't remove fluid already there.

title: Why D

dx.label: THE DIAGNOSIS
dx.name: Renarcotization
dx.text: The naloxone wore off before the methadone did, so the respiratory depression came back.

items: Naloxone's serum half-life in adults is **30–81 minutes**. Methadone's terminal half-life is **8–59 hours**.
**Infusion, not repeat boluses.** A steady level prevents another hypoxic episode between doses.
Infuse about **two-thirds of the effective bolus dose per hour**: 120 mcg → about 80 mcg/h.
Titrate to breathing and sedation, in a **continuously monitored** setting. Not the floor.
! Big fixed doses strip analgesia and can trigger severe pain and a catecholamine surge.
